Italy’s Electric Utilities Industry Sees Stable Trade Activity in First Half of 2024

ROME, June 14 — Italy’s electric utilities industry reported steady trade figures for the first half of 2024, with both imports and exports of electricity holding close to last year’s levels, according to data released Thursday by the National Energy and Grid Authority.

The Authority said Italy imported 24.6 terawatt-hours (TWh) of electricity from neighboring countries between January and June, compared with 24.2 TWh in the same period a year earlier. Exports of electricity reached 8.1 TWh, up slightly from 7.9 TWh in the first half of 2023.

Industry officials described the figures as reflecting “stable and predictable” market conditions, with cross-border flows supported by mild weather and ongoing investments in grid infrastructure.

“Trade volumes remain consistent, and the sector is benefitting from stable demand as well as reliable supply from both domestic generation and our partners in Europe,” said Carlo Bellini, spokesperson for the Italian Association of Electric Utilities.

The figures come as Italy continues gradual integration with the European power market, notably through interconnection projects with France, Switzerland, and Slovenia. The National Energy and Grid Authority noted that the new North Adriatic Interconnector, launched in March, contributed to modest increases in flows from Central Europe.

Wholesale electricity prices for the period averaged €89 per megawatt-hour, little changed from €91 in the same period last year, industry data showed.

Analysts cited the lack of major disruptions or volatility as a positive sign for both consumers and utilities. “The sector is operating under normal conditions, with no significant constraints or shortages,” said Elena Russo, energy analyst at the Milan Energy Institute.

Labor unions also reported routine activity across the country’s main generating and transmission sites. “Operations have proceeded smoothly, with no notable incidents or work stoppages,” said Gianni Lucci, secretary general of the National Utility Workers Union.
